name: GitHub

verdict.topBlocker: Customer organizations block third-party OAuth apps by default; an org owner must approve your app before it can reach private org data.
verdict.summary: Registering an OAuth app is instant and self-serve, with no provider review before any GitHub user can connect. The friction is on the customer side: organizations restrict third-party OAuth apps by default, so an org owner must approve your app before it can reach the org's private repos. Marketplace listing is optional; GitHub publishes no review timeline (community reports say 2–6 weeks).

steps.title: Navigate to GitHub Developer Settings and Create Application
steps.detail: Open Developer Settings under your personal profile or organization account settings. Click 'OAuth apps' and select 'New OAuth App'.

steps.title: Draft Application Metadata and Callback URIs
steps.detail: Fill out the Application Name, Homepage URL, and Authorization Callback URL. GitHub allows up to 10 callback URLs per registered OAuth application.

steps.title: Configure Token Expiration and Device Flow Settings
steps.detail: Ensure token expiration is configured (enabled by default). Enable the Device Flow option if your agent runs in headless environments such as CLI applications.

steps.title: Generate and Secure Client Secret
steps.detail: Generate a new client secret on GitHub. Store the secret securely in your backend environment variables; never embed `client_secret` in client-side code.

steps.title: Construct Authorization Request URL
steps.detail: Build the authorization redirect URL pointing to `https://github.com/login/oauth/authorize` including `client_id`, `redirect_uri`, `scope`, CSRF `state`, and PKCE parameters (`code_challenge` and `code_challenge_method=S256`).

steps.title: Perform Authorization Flow with Test Account
steps.detail: Open the generated authorization link in a web browser signed into a GitHub test account and approve the requested scope permissions.

steps.title: Exchange Authorization Code for Access Token
steps.detail: Receive the temporary code parameter on your redirect URI callback and make a server-side POST request to `https://github.com/login/oauth/access_token` within 10 minutes to obtain an access token.

steps.title: Implement Token Expiration and Refresh Logic
steps.detail: Handle 8-hour access token expiration and store the 6-month refresh token to obtain fresh access tokens when `offline_access` scope or expiring tokens are enabled.

steps.title: Deploy OAuth App to Production
steps.detail: Update your production configuration with the Client ID and backend Client Secret. End users can now connect their GitHub accounts directly without waiting for platform approval.

steps.title: (Optional) Complete Publisher Verification for GitHub Marketplace
steps.detail: If listing your app on GitHub Marketplace, transfer ownership to an organization, enable organization 2FA, verify your domain, and submit a Publisher Verification request.

steps.title: (Optional) Wait for GitHub Marketplace Submission Review
steps.detail: Optional: wait for GitHub to review your Marketplace submission. GitHub does not publish a review timeline; community reports put it at roughly 2–6 weeks.

requirements.note: A personal GitHub account or organization account with administrative access is required to register OAuth applications.
Domain verification is optional for basic OAuth applications, but required if submitting to GitHub Marketplace with Publisher Verification.
Standard GitHub OAuth apps do not undergo mandatory third-party security assessments or manual review pre-approvals.

scopes.note: Grants full access to public and private repositories. Standard GitHub OAuth apps do not require review to request repo scope.
Grants read/write access to user profile data. Does not trigger manual app review.
Grants full management of organization teams, projects, and memberships. Does not trigger manual app review.
Requests expiring access tokens (8 hours) and refresh tokens (6 months). Does not trigger manual review.

blockers.symptom: Users in a customer's organization connect successfully but your agent can't see the org's private repositories.
blockers.cause: OAuth app access restrictions are on by default for new organizations; the app needs org-owner approval.
blockers.unblock: Tell users to request approval during the consent flow (or in Settings → Applications), and ask an org owner to approve it under Organization settings → Third-party access. Consider a GitHub App instead, which orgs install explicitly.

blockers.symptom: Security vulnerability from exposing client_secret in single-page applications
blockers.cause: Attempting to perform the authorization code exchange directly in browser-side JavaScript.
blockers.unblock: Route the code exchange through a secure backend proxy server holding the confidential `client_secret`.

blockers.symptom: Authorization code invalid or expired during token exchange
blockers.cause: The temporary code parameter returned by GitHub expires after 10 minutes or has already been used.
blockers.unblock: Ensure your backend server exchanges the code for tokens immediately upon receiving the callback.

blockers.cause: GitHub OAuth app tokens share the authorizing user's global limit of 5,000 requests per hour.
blockers.unblock: Cache API responses or evaluate building a GitHub App, which provides dedicated installation access tokens that scale with organization size.

claims.text: The GitHub OAuth authorize endpoint redirects requests before validating client_id.
claims.label: tested
claims.method: Sent authorization request with an unknown client_id
claims.artifact:
GET https://github.com/login/oauth/authorize?client_id=oauthready-probe-invalid-client&response_type=code&redirect_uri=https%3A%2F%2Fexample.com%2Fcallback&state=probe (no redirects followed) → HTTP 302
Location: https://github.com/login?client_id=oauthready-probe-invalid-client&return_to=%2Flogin%2Foauth%2Fauthorize%3Fclient_id%3Doauthready-probe-invalid-client%26redirect_uri%3Dhttps%253A%252F%252Fexample.com%252Fcallback%26response_type%3Dcode%26state%3Dprobe

reviewNote: Numbers check out (instant self-serve registration, no provider review). But the real blocker is org owner approval under default-on access restrictions, not client_secret handling. Also, the 2-6 week Marketplace figure in the summary comes only from a community source; official docs give no timeline.
